worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{t},\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,\frac{2}{{t}^{3}},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨\frac{1}{t},\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,0⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,\frac{2}{{t}^{3}},\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{1}{{t}^{3}}-\frac{2}{{t}^{5}} \\  & =-\frac{{t}^{2}+2}{{t}^{5}} \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{t})}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}+\frac{1}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{t}^{2}+1}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}{{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{{t}^{2}+2}{{t}^{5}})}{(\frac{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}{{t}^{2}})} \\  & =-\frac{{t}^{2}+2}{{t}^{3}\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$
html:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by aT=v⋅a||v||.

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows: v=⟨ddt(ln⁡t),ddt(1t),ddt(−1)⟩=⟨1t,−1t2,0⟩

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector: a=⟨ddt(1t),ddt(−1t2),ddt(0)⟩=⟨−1t2,2t3,0⟩

Then, we compute v⋅a and ||v||: v⋅a=⟨1t,−1t2,0⟩⋅⟨−1t2,2t3,0⟩=−1t3−2t5=−t2+2t5||v||=(1t)2+(−1t2)2+(0)2=1t2+1t4=t2+1t4=t2+1t2

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get aT=v⋅a||v||=(−t2+2t5)(t2+1t2)=−t2+2t3t2+1.
